title: Placement diff
description: What one board changes relative to another (RFC 11 Section 6.11): a layout input against a candidate produced from it, or against a later layout input. Derived, never edited, and identified by its content hash. Components are matched by stable identifier.

before.description: The layout input on the before side.

after.description: A candidate produced against the before side's layout input, or a later layout input.

candidate.description: The content hash of the candidate.

components.description: One row per component whose placement differs.

constraints.description: Constraints whose result state or measured value differs. Absent when a side was not checked.

drc.description: Normalized diagnostics present on one side only. Absent when a side was not checked.

copper.description: Traces, vias, and zones present on one side only, by identifier.

Placed.description: Where a component sits on one side: its pose in the board frame and its side. A block member's pose is its block's transform composed with its pose in the block frame (RFC 11 Section 6.1).

refdes.description: The reference designator on the after side, or on the before side for a removed component.

distance.description: The straight-line distance between the two positions, in nanometres, rounded half away from zero. Present when both sides place the component.

block.description: The circuit whose block layout places the component on the after side.

owner.description: The owner of the placement before the change (RFC 12 Section 9.5), or none when there was no placement.

approval.description: What the commit gate's policy will require, when the after side is a candidate. A prediction, not a decision.

Finding.description: A normalized diagnostic (RFC 11 Section 10.3), matched across sides by its code and its entities.
